title: Museum Rietberg: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty Chinese paintings read through rivers, mist, scale and the shape of the sheet.
introduction:
Open paper is not an absence of landscape. In this selection it can carry a river, separate a terrace from a mountain or give a small boat enough room to appear solitary. The inked areas work in relation to those intervals: a densely described bank makes the water beside it more expansive, while a dark contour can establish snow without painting its entire surface.

The works come from the Rietberg’s Chinese painting holdings associated with the Drenowatz collection. Several are album leaves, and two use the curved field of a fan. Those formats matter. These are bounded surfaces with different ways of accommodating a journey, not interchangeable windows onto a single kind of scenery.
visitNote: This is a focused guide to Chinese painting, not a survey of all Rietberg’s collections. Works on paper and silk are sensitive to light and rotate for conservation. Check current displays before visiting; the museum’s collection record establishes a holding, not continuous public exhibition.

books.title: Along the Riverbank: Chinese Paintings from the C. C. Wang Family Collection
books.author: Maxwell K. Hearn and Wen C. Fong (1999)
books.access: Free PDF and online reading from the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
books.note: Hearn and Fong discuss landscape traditions, brushwork, attribution and the history of collecting through works at the Metropolitan Museum. The freely available catalogue offers further context for the older painters named in these album titles.

books.title: How to Read Chinese Paintings
books.author: Maxwell K. Hearn (2008)
books.access: Sample available through the publisher; full book in print.
books.note: This shorter introduction compares individual paintings and calligraphies in detail. The publisher offers a sample; access to the complete book requires a library or purchase.

works.title: Evening by the Jade River
works.catalogueTitle:
Abendstimmung am Jadefluss
Blatt aus dem Album: Die wunderbaren Ansichten von Xuancheng
works.credit: Mei Qing; Museum Rietberg; Foto: Rainer Wolfensberger / Museum Rietberg. Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain (https://data.stadt-zuerich.ch/dataset/mrz_drenowatz_sammlung). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression of the source reproduction.
works.license: Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain
works.description: The river occupies a pale interval between more worked banks. Buildings and distant ridges establish places along it without requiring equal detail throughout. In this leaf from *Views of Xuancheng*, the contrast gives water its breadth. Writing and seals belong to the same sheet, whose space must accommodate more than landscape alone.

works.title: Old Man on a Mule
works.catalogueTitle: Alter Mann auf einem Maultier
works.credit: zugeschrieben: Gao Qipei; Museum Rietberg; Foto: Rainer Wolfensberger / Museum Rietberg. Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain (https://data.stadt-zuerich.ch/dataset/mrz_drenowatz_sammlung). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression of the source reproduction.
works.license: Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain
works.description: A rider and attendant pass through a tall space with few marks to interrupt them. The branch and dark accents provide enough direction for the journey to register. The attribution to Gao Qipei remains qualified; the spareness of the design is something to examine, not evidence sufficient to turn an attributed work into a secure one.

works.title: Seeking the Immortals in the Magu Mountains
works.catalogueTitle:
Auf der Suche nach den Unsterblichen in den Magu-Bergen
Blatt aus dem Album: Die wunderbaren Ansichten von Xuancheng
works.credit: Mei Qing; Museum Rietberg; Foto: Rainer Wolfensberger / Museum Rietberg. Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain (https://data.stadt-zuerich.ch/dataset/mrz_drenowatz_sammlung). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression of the source reproduction.
works.license: Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain
works.description: The search named in the title takes a visible form in overlapping ridges, small buildings and a winding route. No single uninterrupted path explains the whole terrain. The eye has to pass from one mass to the next, making successive encounters within the compact leaf rather than taking possession of the landscape at once.

works.title: On the Terrace of Returning Spring
works.catalogueTitle:
Auf der Terrasse des heimkehrenden Frühlings
Blatt aus dem Album: Die wunderbaren Ansichten von Xuancheng
works.credit: Mei Qing; Museum Rietberg; Foto: Rainer Wolfensberger / Museum Rietberg. Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain (https://data.stadt-zuerich.ch/dataset/mrz_drenowatz_sammlung). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression of the source reproduction.
works.license: Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain
works.description: The terrace and its tree are near; the mountain is distant. Between them lies an interval with much less information. That separation does not break the picture in two. It makes distance an active relation, giving the small foreground position something extensive to face and leaving the passage across it largely unmarked.

works.title: Bamboo and Rocks
works.catalogueTitle:
Bambus und Felsen
Aus einem Album mit Landschaften, Pflanzen und Blumen
works.credit: Hongren; Museum Rietberg; Foto: Rainer Wolfensberger / Museum Rietberg. Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain (https://data.stadt-zuerich.ch/dataset/mrz_drenowatz_sammlung). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression of the source reproduction.
works.license: Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain
works.description: Bamboo and rock are distinguished through the kinds of marks they receive. Pointed leaves gather around slender stems, while broken surfaces give the stone a different resistance. With little colour to separate the subjects, the hand’s change of action becomes especially clear. Open paper gives both room without supplying a detailed background.

works.title: Bamboo Grove on a Cliff
works.catalogueTitle:
Bambushain auf einer Klippe
Aus einem Album mit Landschaften, Pflanzen und Blumen
works.credit: Hongren; Museum Rietberg; Foto: Rainer Wolfensberger / Museum Rietberg. Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain (https://data.stadt-zuerich.ch/dataset/mrz_drenowatz_sammlung). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression of the source reproduction.
works.license: Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain
works.description: A sharply defined cliff sets the small building and bamboo above the lower terrain. Architecture offers a measure of the change in height without taking over the scene. The contrast between hard edges and restrained surface detail makes the ascent intelligible: much can be left undescribed once the main divisions of ground are established.

works.title: Viewing the Waterfall
works.catalogueTitle:
Beim Betrachten des Wasserfalls
Aus dem Album "Lautlose Poesie"
works.medium: Ink and light colour on paper
works.credit: Shen Hao; Museum Rietberg; Foto: Rainer Wolfensberger / Museum Rietberg. Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain (https://data.stadt-zuerich.ch/dataset/mrz_drenowatz_sammlung). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression of the source reproduction.
works.license: Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain
works.description: The small figure on the ledge supplies a second act of viewing inside the picture. Its size gives the waterfall height, while pine and blue-grey rocks distinguish the surrounding spaces. The spectator can follow the figure’s position without needing to inhabit it literally; it is a measure placed within a much larger arrangement.

works.title: Mountain in the Manner of Huang Gongwang
works.catalogueTitle:
Berg im Stil von Huang Gongwang
Aus dem Album: Landschaften im Stil der alten Meister
works.credit: Gu Shanyou; Museum Rietberg; Foto: Rainer Wolfensberger / Museum Rietberg. Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain (https://data.stadt-zuerich.ch/dataset/mrz_drenowatz_sammlung). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression of the source reproduction.
works.license: Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain
works.description: The title openly names Huang Gongwang as a point of reference, so the landscape should not be approached as an isolated invention. Buildings and layered slopes occupy one page while calligraphy faces them. The album presents looking and reading alongside one another, without making the written page merely a caption under an image.

works.title: Mountains and Peaks
works.catalogueTitle:
Berge und Gipfel
Aus dem Album: Landschaften im Stil von Song- und Yuan-Meistern
works.medium: Ink and light colour on paper
works.credit: Zhang Zongcang; Museum Rietberg; Foto: Rainer Wolfensberger / Museum Rietberg. Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain (https://data.stadt-zuerich.ch/dataset/mrz_drenowatz_sammlung). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression of the source reproduction.
works.license: Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain
works.description: Ridges recur with differences in their contour and density of ink. That variation prevents repetition from becoming a row of identical mountains. Small trees and buildings give intervals of scale within the larger masses. The upper inscription also claims part of the open field, keeping the landscape within the physical conditions of an inscribed leaf.

works.title: Bodhidharma Crossing the Yangzi on a Reed
works.catalogueTitle: Bodhidharma Crossing the Yangzi River on a Reed
works.medium: Ink and colour on paper with silk mounting
works.credit: Foto: Rainer Wolfensberger / Museum Rietberg. RCH 1021; Ding Yunpeng; Bodhidharma Crossing the Yangzi River on a Reed; 1574. Complete source image proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no cropping.
works.license: Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain
works.description: The reed is an improbable support for the robed figure. Against the lightly described water, its smallness makes the legendary crossing intelligible as something beyond ordinary balance. The tall format gives the body room while withholding substantial footing. The subject’s marvel is concentrated in that unequal relation rather than a crowded narrative.

works.title: Boat by a Bank with Weeping Willows
works.catalogueTitle:
Boot am Ufer mit Trauerweiden
Aus dem Album: Landschaften im Stil der alten Meister
works.credit: Gu Shanyou; Museum Rietberg; Foto: Rainer Wolfensberger / Museum Rietberg. Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain (https://data.stadt-zuerich.ch/dataset/mrz_drenowatz_sammlung). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression of the source reproduction.
works.license: Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain
works.description: The boat stays near the shelter of slender trees, while hills extend beyond the bank. It is a modest point from which to consider a larger distance. A facing page of calligraphy also slows the encounter: the painting belongs to an album in which attention can alternate between different kinds of mark.

works.title: Mount Lingyan after Snowfall
works.catalogueTitle: Der Berg Lingyan nach dem Schneefall
works.medium: Ink and light colour on paper
works.credit: Museum Rietberg; Foto: Rainer Wolfensberger / Museum Rietberg. Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain (https://data.stadt-zuerich.ch/dataset/mrz_drenowatz_sammlung). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression of the source reproduction.
works.license: Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain
works.description: Snow is suggested by the pale areas left between dark trees and worked mountain contours. The picture does not need to cover the whole sheet in order to describe a covered landscape. The museum record does not establish an artist’s identity; that uncertainty leaves the method available to examine without attaching it to an invented biography.

works.title: Composing Poetry in a Boat beneath a Pine
works.catalogueTitle:
Dichten im Boot im Schatten einer Kiefer
Aus dem Album "Lautlose Poesie"
works.medium: Ink and light colour on paper
works.credit: Shen Hao; Museum Rietberg; Foto: Rainer Wolfensberger / Museum Rietberg. Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain (https://data.stadt-zuerich.ch/dataset/mrz_drenowatz_sammlung). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression of the source reproduction.
works.license: Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain
works.description: The poem itself is not supplied by the seated figures. What is made visible is a situation for composing: a boat beneath an extending pine, with water separated from rock by light marks and colour. The branch provides shelter without filling the entire view. An intellectual activity receives a place rather than a literal illustration of its words.

works.title: A Scholar Viewing a Waterfall
works.catalogueTitle: Ein Gelehrter betrachtet einen Wasserfall
works.credit: Li Liufang; Museum Rietberg; Foto: Rainer Wolfensberger / Museum Rietberg. Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain (https://data.stadt-zuerich.ch/dataset/mrz_drenowatz_sammlung). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression of the source reproduction.
works.license: Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain
works.description: The fan’s boundary changes how much room the landscape has at different points. Small figures and trees occupy a field that widens outward and narrows below, unlike a rectangular sheet. The gold ground is part of that material setting. A waterfall view must be arranged within this shape, not simply cropped from an imagined unlimited scene.

works.title: A Solitary Fisherman
works.catalogueTitle:
Einsamer Fischer
Aus "Album mit Landschaften im Stil alter Meister"
works.credit: Wang Jiu; Museum Rietberg; Foto: Rainer Wolfensberger / Museum Rietberg. Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain (https://data.stadt-zuerich.ch/dataset/mrz_drenowatz_sammlung). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression of the source reproduction.
works.license: Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain
works.description: The river’s pale course turns between densely marked banks. Its narrowing gives distance a direction, while the small boat provides a scale within it. Solitude is therefore a spatial relationship, not a biography assigned to the fisherman. There is considerably more terrain to attend to than human action.

works.title: A Solitary Fisherman on the River
works.catalogueTitle:
Einsamer Fischer am Fluss
Aus einem Album mit Landschaften, Pflanzen und Blumen
works.credit: Hongren; Museum Rietberg; Foto: Rainer Wolfensberger / Museum Rietberg. Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain (https://data.stadt-zuerich.ch/dataset/mrz_drenowatz_sammlung). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression of the source reproduction.
works.license: Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain
works.description: Hongren distributes the scene in low, lightly marked stages rather than building a crowded wall of mountains. A boat remains visible in the broad water between banks and a pavilion. Compare this with Wang Jiu’s fisherman: both use open water, but the different pressure of surrounding ground changes the human figure’s relation to it.

works.title: A Solitary Temple in the Mountains
works.catalogueTitle:
Einsamer Tempel in den Bergen
Aus dem Album: Landschaften im Stil der alten Meister
works.credit: Gu Shanyou; Museum Rietberg; Foto: Rainer Wolfensberger / Museum Rietberg. Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain (https://data.stadt-zuerich.ch/dataset/mrz_drenowatz_sammlung). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression of the source reproduction.
works.license: Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain
works.description: The temple sits within the mountain’s overlapping forms rather than above them as a commanding landmark. Trees and pale distinctions of colour help separate its enclosing terrain. Seclusion can be understood through this arrangement alone: a small built place receives space inside a much larger landscape, without requiring a story about whoever occupies it.

works.title: A Solitary Traveller in a Misty Landscape
works.catalogueTitle:
Einsamer Wanderer in nebelverhangener Landschaft
Aus dem Album: Landschaften im Stil von Song- und Yuan-Meistern
works.medium: Ink and light colour on paper
works.credit: Zhang Zongcang; Museum Rietberg; Foto: Rainer Wolfensberger / Museum Rietberg. Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain (https://data.stadt-zuerich.ch/dataset/mrz_drenowatz_sammlung). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression of the source reproduction.
works.license: Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain
works.description: Pale passages interrupt the more densely described ground between buildings, trees and distant ridges. Mist permits distances to be separated without drawing a hard boundary around each one. The traveller named by the title belongs to this alternation of clarity and concealment; the landscape cannot be read as a completely exposed route.

works.title: A Solitary House in a Marshy River Landscape
works.catalogueTitle: Einsames Haus in sumpfiger Flusslandschaft
works.medium: Fan leaf, ink and colour on gold-ground paper
works.credit: Kuncan; Museum Rietberg; Foto: Rainer Wolfensberger / Museum Rietberg. Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain (https://data.stadt-zuerich.ch/dataset/mrz_drenowatz_sammlung). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression of the source reproduction.
works.license: Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain
works.description: The curved field accommodates buildings, bank and water through changing densities of ink. More concentrated marks establish habitation; thinner passages allow the river to open out. The fan’s interrupted lower boundary is not incidental to the result. It gives the extensive scene a particular shape and requires its distances to fit that surface.

works.title: River Landscape
works.catalogueTitle: Flusslandschaft
works.credit: Dong Qichang; Museum Rietberg; Foto: Rainer Wolfensberger / Museum Rietberg. Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain (https://data.stadt-zuerich.ch/dataset/mrz_drenowatz_sammlung). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression of the source reproduction.
works.license: Museum Rietberg open data: image files public domain
works.description: Angular mountains stand above a broad pale river, with nearer banks and trees forming another stage below. The scene is connected by the spaces between these groups as much as by continuous lines. Following it requires shifts of attention among successive areas, while the inscription takes its own place in the upper field.

closingSections.title: Compare the same subject across different sheets
paragraphs: The two fishermen offer a precise starting point: compare how much space surrounds each boat and how densely the banks are worked. Then compare a rectangular leaf with a fan. The museum’s object records preserve distinctions between dated, attributed and unidentified works; retain them when following links or searching for reproductions. Check current displays separately.
